newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BUMPER SAFRICA '97 WINE PRODUCTION SEEN - KWV CO-OP.
newsitem.headline: BUMPER SAFRICA '97 WINE PRODUCTION SEEN - KWV CO-OP.

text.p: South Africa is expected to have another bumper wine-producing year in 1997, the country's domanant wine co-operative KWV said on Wednesday.
"Indications are that the crop could be about 984 million litres. This will be approximately three perent smaller than last year's record crop," said KWV chairman Jourens Jonker.
"At the moment it seems therefore that the 1997 crop will be the third largest in history," he added, addressing the co-op's annual general meeting.
South African wine sales are currently booming in Britain and other European markets which once shunned the fruit of apartheid.
KWV said earlier this month that South African wine exports increased to 11.1 million cases in 1996, earning the country 550 million rand in foreign exchange.
The co-op, which is based in Paarl in the Cape winelands, revised its initial estimates for 1995 exports to 8.2 million cases, up from an initial 7.7 million cases.
Exports had swelled by 1,300 percent from the 855,000 cases in 1990, it said.
South African wine is exported to around 60 countries, with the European Union the biggest single foreign consumer.
